title: GPU spot vs reserve hedge and HC swing matrix (Apr 2026)
summary: Working spreadsheet for modeling hybrid GPU procurement (spot vs reserved), headcount hiring swings by role, and resulting pricing sensitivity on hosted API unit economics and runway. Primary goal: recommend an operational hedge mix + hiring cadence to protect a 9-12 month runway under price shock scenarios.
body:
Context:
- We need a defensible procurement + hiring hedge that preserves product SLAs while protecting runway if spot prices spike or reserved capacity lead times grow.
- This sheet models 3 procurement mixes (Base / Spot-heavy / Reserve-heavy) and 3 hiring cadences (Aggressive hire, Baseline, Hiring freeze) and runs price-shock sensitivity +/-20% on effective GPU-hour costs plus 15% attrition shock.

Key assumptions (inputs):
- Baseline throughput (tokens/month): 1200M tokens
- Avg token compute per 1K tokens -> 0.012 GPU-hours (model mix weighted)
- Baseline GPU-hour cost (blend): $2.50/hr (spot portion $1.40, reserved equivalent $3.40 amortized)
- Monthly reserved commit pricing available with 12-month term, 30% discount vs on-demand; prepay credits reduce variable cost by additional 8% for Q3-Q4.
- Hiring salaries (fully loaded monthly): Infra Eng $25k, Serving Eng $22k, SRE $20k, Product/PM $18k, Finance Ops $12k.
- Recruiting lead: 8 weeks average; hiring freeze reduces ramp hires to 0 for modeling months.
- Token price (hosted API revenue per 1K tokens): $0.55 (current avg).

Scenarios (rows are monthly aggregates):
| Scenario | GPU hours (monthly) | GPU cost/mo | New FTEs/mo | FTE cost/mo | Total spend/mo | Unit cost per 1M tokens | Runway impact (delta months) | Notes |
|---------|---------------------:|------------:|------------:|-----------:|--------------:|------------------------:|-------------------------:|------|
| Base (50/50 spot/reserve) | 14,400 | $36,000 | 3 | $195,000 | $231,000 | $192.5 | 0 | baseline
| Spot-heavy (70% spot) | 14,400 | $29,280 | 5 | $325,000 | $354,280 | $295.2 | -1.6 | cheaper GPU cost but higher variance
| Reserve-heavy (80% reserved) | 14,400 | $44,160 | 2 | $130,000 | $174,160 | $145.1 | +1.2 | higher fixed costs but price stability

Sensitivity matrix (effect on monthly GPU cost only):
- Spot price +20%: Base GPU cost -> $39,840 (+10.7% from baseline), Spot-heavy -> $33,936 (+15.9%), Reserve-heavy -> $44,160 (unchanged)
- Spot price -20%: Base GPU cost -> $32,160 (-10.7%), Spot-heavy -> $24,624 (-15.9%), Reserve-heavy unchanged
- Attrition shock +15% (increases hiring/replacement costs): additional monthly FTE cost estimate +$12k to +$45k depending on hires replaced mid-quarter.

Per-role hiring swings (quarterly cumulative view):
| Role | Current FTEs | Aggressive hire (Q2 add) | Baseline (Q2 add) | Freeze | Notes |
|------|-------------:|------------------------:|------------------:|-------:|------|
| Infra Eng | 18 | +6 | +2 | 0 | infra needed for private deployments/dedicated pool ops
| Serving Eng | 26 | +8 | +3 | 0 | runtime and model onboarding
| SRE | 10 | +4 | +1 | 0 | latency/incident coverage for Dedicated
| Product/PM | 8 | +2 | +1 | 0 | rollout support for Dedicated/Private
| Finance Ops | 6 | +1 | 0 | 0 | capacity to run pricing experiments and billing ops

Quarterly cost snapshots (example numbers):
- Aggressive hire + Spot-heavy (combined): GPU cost Q = $90k, FTE incremental cost Q = $420k, one-time recruiting/ONB = $60k, total Q = $570k. Unit cost per 1M tokens jumps to ~$360. Runway shortens by ~2.6 months vs baseline.
- Reserve-heavy + Freeze: GPU cost Q = $132k (commits amortized), FTE incremental cost Q = $0, total Q = $132k. Unit cost per 1M tokens ~$110. Runway extends by ~1.4 months.

Pricing sensitivity to hosted API price change (impact on margin/runway):
- If hosted token price drops 10% (to $0.495 per 1K tokens): baseline margin before fixed ops drops by ~9%, runway shortens by ~1.1 months.
- If hosted token price increases 15% due to packaging changes: runway extends by ~1.6 months under Reserve-heavy.

Actionable recommendations (draft):
1) Adopt a "tactical hybrid" procurement: target 60% reserved for critical latency paths (serving-critical models), 40% spot for batch/low-priority workloads. Keeps effective GPU-hours near baseline cost but reduces downside variance.
2) Implement a 2-quarter hiring pause for non-customer-facing roles (Product/Finance Ops hires delayed 8–12 weeks) while allowing 40% of planned infra/serving hires to proceed (prioritize senior ICs).
3) Establish prepay credit pilot for Q3 (commit $1.5M in prepay) to capture the additional ~8% variable cost reduction during the seasonally high-demand window.
4) Run an immediate stress-test: repeat this model with spot price +40% and a 25% attrition scenario to prepare escalation triggers (threshold: runway reduction >3 months).
5) Add tagging in billing/console to split serving-critical requests vs background so routing policies can be applied (move low-priority to spot cluster).

Open questions / to do:
- Get updated committed-reserve quotes from cloud partners for 1/3/12-month terms (Liam) [JIRA-FF-4123].
- Validate token compute-per-1K assumption with Serving runtime team (Dustin).
- Legal review on prepay credit contract clauses (Olivia).
- Product ops: identify top 3 features that must maintain latency SLAs if we shift to spot-heavy for background workloads.

Notes (draft tone):
- This is an early working model; numbers are rounded and should be treated as directional.
- The matrix favors reserve-heavy for runway preservation but reduces flexibility and increases capital commitment risk. Spot-heavy improves near-term cashflow but amplifies tail risk for price shocks. Hybrid 60/40 is a pragmatic compromise recommended for review.

Checklist before finalizing: [ ] refresh model with latest cloud quotes, [ ] run 12-month Monte Carlo with demand variance, [ ] finance leadership sign-off, [ ] present to execs 2026-05-03.

Comments log (working):

- 2026-04-18 Olivia: flagged contract risk on prepay; ask Legal.

End of sheet (draft).
